places.name: Douglas Municipal Terminal
places.notes: Stays where it is on City land, facing the apron. The jet parks airside at Gate A2; the player walks in through today's door (94,-39), reads the terminal in arrival order (Marcus at Gate A2, Dana at the charter desk, Lupe at Sky Cafe, Officer Dale, Rosa at the desk, the 1928 wall) and leaves through a NEW landside door on the north-east end face, then walks 55 m under the Sun Gate into Arrivals Court. The landside door is a City decision.

places.name: Gate A2 jet stand (today's arrivals plaza)
places.notes: Today's Flight Line hub and airside arrivals plaza become the stand where the jet parks, with visiting jets on the paved stands beside it. Cart rental and the six Sikk cruisers move landside to the Cart and Bike Hub; both terminal balloons move to Stratos Field (no balloons beside an active runway).

places.name: The Tower (City control tower)
places.notes: The City's tower and overlook. Nothing of ours is built here.

places.name: Hangar Row (City flight line)
places.notes: The City's flight line hangars stay as airport scenery, seen from the Flight Deck. The parked jets move off the taxiways onto paved stands.

places.name: 1928 Airfield Museum (City of Douglas)
places.notes: The airport's own museum in a white bow-truss hangar beside the Tower: the story of the 1928 international airfield. A City item, reached landside on the Museum Walk from Link Plaza.

places.name: Sky Rings (jet minigame)
places.notes: Still launched from the jet at Gate A2; the ring course is re-hung inside the section over our land only.

places.name: Link Plaza (north head of the Flight Line Link)
places.notes: A plain City walk and the covered ramp head on City land beside Terminal Drive; the fountain and the kiosk stand on our land at the Arrivals Court end of the Landside Walk. A City item, subject to City of Douglas approval (decision 2).

places.name: Flight Line Link (underpass to Stage Two)
places.notes: Covered walk and cart underpass, 10 m wide, under the main taxiway: 230 m from ramp head to ramp head, 85 m ramps at 1 in 13 and a 60 m covered box from z 30 to 90 (the taxiway pavement spans z 51 to 69). About 170 m of it and its north ramp lie on City land, so it is a City item by agreement (decision 2). 242 m from the runway centreline at its closest. The Flight Line Tug heritage tram on Terminal Drive and N Airport Rd is the day-one alternative.

places.name: Runway Hall (inside The Crossing)
places.notes: The widened middle of The Crossing, directly under the runway centreline: an LED ceiling shows the jet rolling overhead in real time, the floor hums, the 1928 timeline ends here and the frontier begins.

places.name: Arrivals Court
places.notes: The first step on our land. The Sun Gate shell over the walk from the landside door, the Welcome Fountain (a three-tier cantera fountain whose tiers are shallow spill lips over floor jets and a flush grated drain, 262 m from the runway), the kiosk map, the taxi and shuttle kerb of Terminal Drive on its north-west edge, Sky the tour guide. Run by The Landing Club as its arrivals forecourt. Across the airfield, 1.3 km away, the Genesis Ring stands on the horizon.

places.name: The Sun Gate
places.notes: 14 m white tensile shell framing the Sun Gate Walk from the new landside terminal door into Arrivals Court. Single storey equivalent, fabric on steel masts.

places.name: Welcome House
places.notes: Clubhouse-operated arrivals lounge at the head of the Club Walk: concierge, the scale model of Genesis One, the Founders Row lot desk. The gallery model re-textured in cream stucco and aluminium.

places.name: Cart and Bike Hub
places.notes: Clubhouse-operated: cart rental and the six Sikk cruisers move here from the airside plaza, into a hangar kitbash on the Terminal Drive kerb.

places.name: Founders' Cache (treasure hunt start)
places.notes: Moves off the airport apron. Starts at Arrivals Court and hides one cache per chapter along the Horizon Line.

places.name: Club Walk arcade
places.notes: A two-sided streamline arcade on the Horizon Line: 15 storefronts at 14 m pitch under a continuous shade canopy (club store, Sky Cafe annex, outfitter, pilot shop, Giveback desk, gallery), the Welcome House at its head and a gap on the airfield side for the Flight Deck spur. Operated by The Landing Club as clubhouse amenities.

places.name: The Flight Deck
places.notes: The club's plane-spotting bar and terrace at the fence, 168 m from the runway centreline, looking down the runway. The art pavilion model re-set as a single-storey bar, long side to the runway.

places.name: Airfield Amphitheater
places.notes: The club's small outdoor stage, moved out of the Landing Wash and off the Crossing Lane to the airfield side of the Club Walk, so the runway is its backdrop.

places.name: Crossing Plaza (north portal)
places.notes: Top of the north ramp of The Crossing: a 1928 biplane on a plinth, a replica airport beacon (static and unlit), the Rabbit fountain, and the Crossing Shuttle platform. Service and the Grand Loop reach it on the Crossing Lane from Landing Boulevard, never on a taxi-street.

places.name: The Crossing (runway underpass)
places.notes: Cut-and-cover box under the City parallel taxiway and Runway 03/21 at runway station t -450: straight and perpendicular to the runway under the pavement, 225 m covered (s +112 to -112), 85 m ramps at 1 in 13 on both sides and both ramps on our land; the last 40 m of the south ramp curve 23.5 degrees right onto the Main Street axis, so you climb out facing the Ring. 14 m wide: a moving walkway and the Crossing Shuttle lane (it boards automatically at both portals, so the 460 m is a ride, not a march), with the Runway Hall at the middle. Needs City of Douglas and FAA approval. Fallback: the Nort

places.name: Founders Row (the Stage One airpark)
places.notes: The 24 founders lots come home from north of the section road as the hangar-home lots of Stage One, now at 42 m spacing: on the Landing Taxilane, Rudder Way, Propeller Way and Wingtip Way (residents' taxi-streets behind hold lines). Hangar doors face the taxi frontage, front doors face the street, gardens face the desert. Through-the-fence gates TTF-1 and TTF-2 are proposals for the City to designate.

places.name: Founders Row lot office (Elena)
places.notes: Elena's lot office at the head of Founders Lane, beside Crossing Plaza, in a re-textured storefront.

places.name: Club Hangars
places.notes: Three shared storage hangars for members and visiting aircraft at the north-east tip, at runway stations t -905 to -955, run by the club, below the approach and transitional surfaces. No fuel is sold anywhere on our land.

places.name: The Landing Clubhouse
places.notes: Kept in place: clubhouse, pool and terrace facing south over the Club Green to the runway. The social heart of Stage One.

places.name: Club Ramp
places.notes: Fly-in guest parking beside the clubhouse, reached from Propeller Way; two visiting jets tie down here. The Club Loop and Club Lane end short of it at gates.

places.name: The Chapel
places.notes: Moves 355 m from the taxiway edge (where hangar homes now go) to the Pavilion Green, so the Chapel and the Grand Pavilion form one wedding and gathering lawn. Pastor Joe moves with it.

places.name: The Grand Pavilion
places.notes: Kept: the club's events pavilion; its white peaks are the Stage One landmark from the air.

places.name: North Gate
places.notes: Stage One gate monument 15 m inside the North Section Road; the club entrance by car and the Grand Loop's way out.

places.name: Airpark Gate (residents)
places.notes: Residents' and guests' gate on Skyline Lane, moved west so it no longer opens onto the Wingtip Way taxi-street.

places.name: Flight Line Gate
places.notes: The front door by road from the town of Douglas on N Airport Rd; gold stage-colour monument inside the road.

places.name: Flight Line Market
places.notes: Two rows of storefronts: the north row faces Flight Line Road, the south row faces The Flight Line promenade, with the market hall between them (Parcel 1 commercial and retail use). Visitor parking behind the south row.

places.name: The Pilot House (pilot lounge)
places.notes: Pilot lounge, flight planning and crew rest on Propeller Plaza: a streamline moderne kitbash of the diner and hangar models.

places.name: Flight Line Diner
places.notes: Moves off the City tarmac onto the north edge of our Stage Two apron; tables face the main taxiway. It is Parcel 1's restaurant.

places.name: Propeller Plaza
places.notes: The Stage Two threshold where the Flight Line Link comes up: the Propeller Fountain (pool-less floor jets under a turning propeller), vintage aircraft on plinths, the Pilot House, and the doors of the flight school and maintenance hangar across the apron.

places.name: Flight Line T-hangars (rental)
places.notes: Today's runway-side hangars regroup as a row of four low-bay rental T-hangars along the south edge of the existing paved slab (x -100 to 22, z 120 to 208), doors to the apron.

places.name: Flight Line Maintenance (maintenance and avionics)
places.notes: Maintenance and avionics hangar on the north edge of the slab, doors to the apron.

places.name: Flight Line Flight School
places.notes: Flight school hangar and classroom on the north edge of the slab; the trainers tie down in the aisle.

places.name: Aircraft wash pad
places.notes: Shaded wash pad beside the TTF-3 link. No fuel is sold anywhere on our land.

places.name: Giveback Shop
places.notes: Stays in its hangar on Hangar Lane.

places.name: Hangar Lane shops
places.notes: Pilot supply, flight gear, the model shop and the Giveback Shop on the north-west side of Hangar Lane, facing Flight Line Row.

places.name: Flight Line Row hangar homes
places.notes: 6 hangar homes at 42 m pitch on the Flight Line Taxilane, between the T-hangars and the Mesquite Fingers (hangar doors to the taxilane at s 112, front doors to Hangar Lane, houses past the 130 m line and 8 m high to stay under the transitional surface).

places.name: The Paddock
places.notes: Start line, timing hut, pits (two barn garages) and the grandstand serving both the drag strip and the Cart Course. Dee the marshal.

places.name: Drag Strip (eighth mile)
places.notes: Today's 320 m strip ran into the runway safety area. It becomes a 270 m strip (eighth mile plus shutdown and a sand arrestor bed) in the corridor between the west windrow and the first Mesquite Finger, launching at the Paddock and running south, away from the houses of Douglas, 70 m inside N Airport Rd behind a 4 m planted berm, with noise hours (no runs after 21:00). It ends 190 m from the runway centreline. Leaderboard resets.

places.name: Cart Course
places.notes: Today's six-gate oval at 0.75 scale (180 by 162 m, gates from x -390 to -210 around (-300,282)), moved onto the old graded pad clear of the Mesquite Fingers and the drag strip.

places.name: Fingers Lap (cart trail)
places.notes: The Lake Lap time trial becomes a loop through the Mesquite Fingers.

places.name: Threshold Overlook
places.notes: Plane-spotting shade pavilion and kiosk near the Runway 03 end, outside the runway protection zone, on the Fingers trail.

places.name: Expanse Gate (south portal)
places.notes: Top of the curved south ramp: you surface facing the Frontier Arch, Main Street and the Genesis Ring dead ahead. The Frontier Well fountain, the relic 1928 Strip running east and west, frontier storefronts framing the plaza. People only: the shuttle and cars stop at the Arcade Bay 90 m east and the Garden Bay 60 m west.

places.name: Genesis Arcade
places.notes: Moved 77 m north-east off the Expanse Gate (rotation kept): as you surface it stands off your left shoulder, and its doors open onto the Night Walk.

places.name: Arcade Bay
places.notes: Where Night Field Road and the Stage Road end: a turning circle with the Grand Loop and taxi stop, 90 m from the Frontier Well. A windpump on the island.

places.name: The 1928 Strip
places.notes: The relic crosswind runway kept as a promenade, threshold numbers repainted, windsock, stagecoach stop at the east end.

places.name: Community Garden
places.notes: Kept at the west end of the 1928 Strip; its solar arrays move to the North Yard.

places.name: Expanse Depot
places.notes: Shuttle and cart barn (two barn models and a hangar kitbash), service yard and the rover fleet for The Outpost, on Night Field Road (Parcel 3 industrial use).

places.name: Utility Yard
places.notes: Water, wastewater package plant, power and a public safety post (three low shed kitbashes) behind a 4 m planted berm, 70 m inside the east edge.

places.name: Solar Field
places.notes: The solar arrays regrouped in a screened compound 290 m to the side of the extended runway centreline, anti-reflective panels, glare study against the Runway 21 approach before anything is built.

places.name: Launch Complex car park
places.notes: Event parking off Night Field Road so cars never enter the town; a ticket booth at its gate.

places.name: The Ring geoglyph
places.notes: Approach land art: a 90 m Genesis Ring laid in coloured gravel at the north tip, flat on the ground, readable from the Runway 21 final approach, outside the runway protection zone.

places.name: Frontier Arch
places.notes: Timber arch over the head of Main Street; it frames the Ring.

places.name: Four Corners
places.notes: Main Street crosses the Old Track Parkway and Corral Road on a raised slow table, on dry ground 110 m from the arroyo's flow line. The Douglas Bank, the Grand Hotel, the Four Corners Saloon and the General Store stand on its four corners, with the horse trough fountain. Cars cross, never drive along Main Street.

places.name: Main Street
places.notes: Rebuilt on the Horizon Line axis (bearing 154) from the Expanse Gate to Compass Plaza: continuous false fronts at 13 m pitch on both boardwalks, the stagecoach depot and trading post at the head, Four Corners, the timber Arroyo Bridge, and the territorial courthouse and assay office at the foot. A pedestrian-first shared street: carts, bikes and the stagecoach only. Priya keeps the Grand Hotel desk; Tomas and his General Store move in from off the land; Hank tends bar in the Four Corners Saloon.

places.name: Compass Plaza
places.notes: The hub at the end of Main Street: Compass Fountain inside a 120 m compass rose geoglyph that reads from the air, and the Outpost Beacon on its east edge, the first off-world object on the street.

places.name: The Outpost Beacon
places.notes: A 5 m meteorite-shaped monolith with a slow cyan core on the east edge of Compass Plaza, off the axis: the first sign of the off-world stage on the walk from Main Street.

places.name: The Seven Gates (Sculpture Avenue)
places.notes: Seven corten frames stepping down in size that frame the Ring.

places.name: Artist studios
places.notes: Studios and galleries regrouped along the Gallery Walk and Gallery Lane, every gallery footprint at least 30 m from the Arrivals Court sightline to the Ring.

places.name: The Design District sculpture fields
places.notes: Today's monoliths, corten pieces, Untitled (Ring), Reeds in Corten and Sun Stone set out as sculpture fields along the Gallery Walk, all under 6 m. Mateo the curator.

places.name: Field of Light
places.notes: Thousands of glowing stems on the open desert, lit after dark. Low (under 1 m).

places.name: Sun Tunnels
places.notes: Four concrete tubes aligned to the solstice sunrise and sunset, on a 36 m spur from Studio Lane.

places.name: Stone Spiral
places.notes: Basalt spiral laid in the Ridge Arroyo where the Ridge Walk crosses the wash.

places.name: The Flagship Pavilion
places.notes: Kept: the signature pavilion on the Gallery Walk.

places.name: The Genesis Lodge
places.notes: The flagship stay: a low-rise courtyard resort (two hotel wings and lodge villas around a private pool court) between the Gallery Walk and the Field of Light, its terrace facing the Ring. The lobby is the one Meshy hero model of the plan.

places.name: Outpost Gate
places.notes: Where the Horizon Line crosses Ridge Road: beyond this line no wheels but rovers. Countdown ring 10 stands here.

places.name: Launch Plaza
places.notes: Launch Mist fountain, the lander sculpture 25 m east of the axis, rover stop.

places.name: Mission Control
places.notes: The Outpost visitor centre facing Launch Plaza, astronaut guide; mission briefings in its forecourt bowl.

places.name: The Genesis Dome (The Ascent)
places.notes: The Ascent becomes a Genesis Dome-scale landmark: a low-profile 60 m geodesic biome, 18 m high, with a planetarium, mission hall and biome garden, moved to (833,752) so its centre stands 68 m west of the Arrivals Court sightline and 111 m off the Main Street axis.

places.name: The Genesis Ring
places.notes: A low, wide landmark ring, never a tower: 24 m across, set on its edge on a low mound over the Halo Mist, steady cyan glow that cannot be mistaken for airport lighting. Needs an FAA Form 7460-1 review; decision 4 offers 12 m, 24 m and 36 m options.

places.name: Habitat One (dome stays)
places.notes: The geodesic domes of the Glamping Field and South Ridge become a crescent of habitat pods on the Habitat Crescent, outside the Orbit Walk (hospitality keys).

places.name: Stratos Field
places.notes: Three balloons fly from here every day (two more on event days), 1 km from the runway. The Balloon Race is a guided free flight along the south and east edge to about (1100,650) through rings at 20 to 45 m, suspended while an aircraft is in the pattern (the same logic as the Landing Light Pause). It sits under the Runway 21 downwind leg, so it needs airport coordination.

places.name: Low-G Course
places.notes: The sixteen floating platforms re-themed as a low gravity course. Milo moves with it.

places.name: Dark Sky Observatory
places.notes: In the south-east corner, 1.2 km from the runway lights. The Ring, the Countdown and the Orbit Walk are shielded downlights and dim to a minimum for the dark-sky hour after the last rover. Dr. Vega.

places.name: Crater Row
places.notes: Off-world themed dome homes on a crescent lane inside The Outpost (future, subject to rezoning).

places.name: Homestead Domes
places.notes: Dome homesteads on Homestead Lane, the strip the Outpost takes from the Frontier Ranches between Spur Lane and Ridge Road (future, subject to rezoning).

places.name: Frontier Ranch
places.notes: Working desert ranch between the Launch Complex wash and the Expanse Arroyo: barns, stables, a windmill, horses, the livery for the stagecoach. Wyatt.

places.name: The Corral
places.notes: Rodeo arena, grandstands, chutes, saloon and barn at the end of Corral Road, trailers from the Corral Gate on the East Section Road. The Bull ride and the Rodeo arena come with it.

places.name: Frontier Ranches
places.notes: Ranch homes with barns on Ranch Lane, Stirrup Lane and Lariat Lane (renamed from West Ranches so the name does not point the wrong way). Future, subject to rezoning.

places.name: Launch Complex Plaza
places.notes: The off-world stage starts here, 340 m from the tunnel mouth: the countdown clock, the food hall and ticket booths, the dancing light fountain, and the doors of the Crater Bowl and the Star Cinema.

places.name: Crater Bowl
places.notes: The Concert Bowl re-themed as a crater amphitheater: stage on its north-west side, LED wall facing south-east away from the Runway 21 final approach, behind a 4 m earth berm (broken where the wash passes), brightness capped, and the show holds its lighting while an aircraft is on approach (the Landing Light Pause). Runway frame t -832, s -305: alongside the runway, not beyond the threshold. The Dance Battle floor moves with it.

places.name: Star Cinema
places.notes: The Drive-In re-themed as the Star Cinema: 42 m screen facing south-east, its back to the runway, behind the same berm; runway frame t -730, s -332, clear of the wash. AV Hub and Snack Shack move with it.

places.name: Maker Row and Expanse Works
places.notes: Maker workshops and light industrial along both sides of Hangar Road, 181 to 235 m from the runway centreline (Parcel 3 industrial use). There is no taxiway on this side, so these are workshops, not aircraft storage.

places.name: South Hangar Row (Maker Row workshops)
places.notes: The seven South Hangar Row hangars move back from the runway (from about s -118 to s -194) into the Maker Row as workshops, outside the 150 m line and under the 7:1 transitional surface.

places.name: Mesa Heights
places.notes: Desert-modern homes on Mesa Loop behind the west side of Main Street, re-planned north-west of the Old Track Parkway; the North Mesa houses join them on North Mesa Lane. Future, subject to rezoning.

places.name: North Mesa Lane
places.notes: North Mesa comes home from 1.4 km off the land as the middle lane of Mesa Heights (casitas, villas, ranch homes). Future, subject to rezoning.

places.name: Sunset Bluff
places.notes: West-facing homes on Bluff Loop over the runway. Future, subject to rezoning.

places.name: The Commons
places.notes: Kept: glamping village square and pool homes; Ada hosts.

places.name: The Fireside
places.notes: The 32-log fire circle moves into The Commons, clear of the Old Track Parkway.

places.name: Commons glamping loop
places.notes: The off-site Glamping Field merges into The Commons glamping loop.

places.name: Fountain Court
places.notes: The seven lake houses (the Founder's and Dev's) and two manors re-set as courtyard estates around the Grand Cascade, stepped stone runnels over a flush grated drain with no pool. Nate becomes the Fountain Court host. Future, subject to rezoning.

places.name: Lakeside man-made lake, docks and ponds
places.notes: Cut: open water breaks the brand rule and it sat 445 m off the land. The lake terraces and the Lake Lap go with it.

places.name: South Ridge
places.notes: Moves 390 m west along the south edge to free the corner for The Outpost. Future, subject to rezoning.

places.name: Desert Golf (the Short Six)
places.notes: Six desert par-3 holes in the band t 470 to 820, s -205 to -335: every tee and landing area at least 200 m from the runway centreline with netting on the runway side, 80 m from the AWOS mast and 50 m from the South Section Road. Replaces nine holes spread over 440 m off the land. Driving Range on the far side hitting away from the runway, Putting Green on the clubhouse terrace.

places.name: Golf clubhouse, range and putting green
places.notes: Single-storey clubhouse (inside the AWOS circle) set back from Golf Road, facing the Clubhouse Terrace and its fountain. Coach Bo.

places.name: AWOS weather station
places.notes: Planning placement at runway frame t 449, s -185: its 305 m circle sits entirely inside the section (0.0 ac on neighbours' land) and holds only single-storey uses (golf, casitas, glamping, workshops). Reached on a 36 m service spur from Hangar Road. The recorded easement position must replace this before any Stage Three core content is placed.

places.name: Field 1 (the City diamond)
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The existing full-size diamond, home plate at (-448,-442) facing north-east, the fence about 100 m out. Upgraded: six 18 m LED light poles with full cut-off heads (off by 10 pm), a 300-seat grandstand under a shade roof laid along the first-base line on the foul side (36 by 8 m, 5 m off the line, clear of the infield), dugouts, a new backstop and netting, a scoreboard in right-centre, and the scorers' booth at the grandstand's east end. Coach Ray runs Friday night games.

places.name: Field 2 (Little League)
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The rough north practice field re-laid as a Little League diamond (200 ft fences) with home plate at its south-east corner, about (-272,-440), facing north-west: its outfield and Field 1's back onto each other across the Fields Walk behind a shared fence, so neither field's home runs land in the other. Four 15 m LED poles; bleachers on its east and south lines.

places.name: North Meadow (practice turf)
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The rest of the practice field kept as open turf: team practice, flag football, kite flying.

places.name: Pump Track
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The small dirt track read at the top of the practice field (its use to be confirmed with the City) rebuilt as an asphalt pump track for bikes, scooters and boards.

places.name: Tailwind Dog Park
places.notes: Two fenced yards (big dogs and small dogs) with a double-gated entry off the Loop, shade sails, a dog-wash station and the Hydrant fountain, with the pump track and the North Meadow between it and the farm's livestock.

places.name: Airport Park car park
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The existing paved car park, kept: resurfaced, shade trees in new planted islands (the posts stand on them), a drop-off and bus bay at the east end, and its west 14 m rebuilt as a planted island that carries the Loop over Airport Park Drive on a raised crossing.

places.name: North car park
places.notes: About 20 spaces on the old gravel strip by the North Section Road, inside the City's parcel line and 6 m clear of the Loop, for the dog park, the pump track and the farm.

places.name: The Great Lawn
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The existing big grass field (about 225 by 100 m), kept as turf: a youth soccer pitch either side of the Bandshell Walk on weekend mornings, the town picnic, movie nights, and on concert nights the whole lawn in front of the Bandshell. The Loop runs along its south and west sides, the Lawn Walk up its east edge and the Bandshell Walk up its centre line.

places.name: The Bandshell
places.notes: A copper-lined timber shell on the lawn's north edge, its back to the old tree row, facing south down the Bandshell Walk: the audience has the sunset on its left rather than in its eyes, the sound carries south over empty land toward the airfield and away from the houses, and the stage lights point north, away from the runway.

places.name: The Park House
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The City's restrooms, concession and big ramada behind the tree row, fronting the lawn, kept and refreshed; the park office and first aid move in here.

places.name: South car park
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The existing dirt lot by Red Roof Hall, paved as a car park of about 40 spaces north of the realigned Terminal Drive and entered from it by the South Lot Lane.

places.name: Red Roof Hall
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The City's red-roofed building, kept (its use today to be confirmed with the City), fronting Terminal Drive; proposed as the park's meeting hall and team room.

places.name: Windmill Green
places.notes: The park's crossroads, where the Farm Walk and the Lawn Walk meet the Cottonwood Walk: a steel windpump spilling into a stone trough, the City's two old white shade ramadas kept and re-roofed as its shelters, restrooms and the kiosk; the Hangar Playground and the splash pad on one side, the barn in view up the Farm Walk.

places.name: Hangar Playground
places.notes: An adventure playground with a little airfield theme: the Little Hangar (a bow-truss climbing frame with slides and a rope net), the master plan's 1928 biplane re-used as a climb-aboard, the Little Runway (a balance-bike and trike loop with painted 03 and 21 numbers), a propeller spinner and balloon swings; the small play set by the south lot moves here.

places.name: Propeller Splash Pad
places.existing: Airport Park (City of Douglas, real and used today; not built in the game yet)
places.notes: The small round blue basin by the car park (probably a splash pad today) rebuilt as a toddler splash pad with a turning propeller sprinkler; the City's splash-court ramada beside it is kept.

places.name: Mesquite Grove
places.notes: Two bookable group ramadas and family tables under the mesquite bosque, grills and horseshoe pits: where Douglas throws its birthday parties.

places.name: Splash Meadow House
places.notes: Restrooms and changing rooms for the Splash Meadow, the Splash Meadow's own treatment plant and tank, and the creek's pump room above a buried 150 cubic metre cistern.

places.name: Genesis Barn
places.notes: The farm's red gambrel barn (8 m to the ridge), facing south down the Farm Walk: stalls, a hay loft, the farm classroom and barn dances. Farmer Marisol hosts.

places.name: The Barnyard
places.notes: The yard in front of the barn: the Barnyard Pump, the Farm Stand, the Saturday farm market, hay-bale seats, hand-wash stations at every exit; every pen drinks from automatic waterers, never an open trough.

places.name: Petting Yard
places.notes: Goats, sheep, rabbits, chickens and a donkey behind a low fence with an attendant; open set hours, the animals rest in the barn the other hours; hand-wash stations at the gate.

places.name: Cattle paddock
places.notes: A cow and calf in the paddock and Duke the bull behind a double fence, with a field shelter.

places.name: Sheep, goat and pig paddocks
places.notes: Split paddocks along the Paddock Path, with the chicken run and the farm dog keeping an eye on the sheep.

places.name: Kitchen Garden
places.notes: Raised beds of chile, squash, beans and corn run with local schools, the corn always under netting; what grows here is sold at the Farm Stand, beside the tortoise garden.

places.name: Heritage Orchard
places.notes: Apple, pomegranate, fig and pecan trees on drip irrigation: blossom in March, picking in the autumn, windfalls cleared daily.

places.name: Genesis Spring
places.notes: Where the creek begins: a basalt and limestone grotto at the old scraped pad read from the aerial (probably an old stock tank), ferns and monkeyflower on its seep face, the water welling up through a boulder bed into a shallow spill basin and out over a stone lip into the creek. The Hummingbird Garden (chuparosa, penstemon, desert honeysuckle) surrounds Spring Terrace. Ranger Luis tells the story of the springs every ranch in the valley grew from.

places.name: Willow Reach and the Riffle Stones
places.notes: Braided riffles over gravel bars under Goodding willow, bunchgrass to the water's edge; the Riffle Stones cross here from the Creek Walk to the Loop. Dragonflies over the riffles by day (the creek is UV-treated, never chlorinated).

places.name: Sacaton Meadow
places.notes: A drip-watered meadow of big sacaton and deergrass, the dry-side cousin of the cienegas of the San Bernardino Ranch east of Douglas: the creek crosses it in one narrow planted channel, with no sedges, no wetland plants, no wet ground and no ponded water, so it never becomes a marsh that draws waterfowl, herons or cranes. The Sacaton Boardwalk crosses it on the Willow Bridge.

places.name: The Confluence
places.notes: Where the Landing Run from Stage One meets Genesis Creek, just below the Confluence Bridge, with Cottonwood Falls upstream: the Confluence Terrace on the east bank, the park totem and a kiosk.

places.name: Splash Meadow and the Sink
places.notes: The children's play water, on the west bank beside the creek's foot: a flat stone terrace with ground jets, stepping stones and a play stream where hand pumps and sluice gates let children dam and release their own little creek, zero depth, on its own sealed and treated splash-pad circuit and tank, like the Propeller Splash Pad. The creek runs past its east edge behind a low planted bank and, a few metres on, fans out over a cobble bar and sinks into the ground at the Sink, as desert streams do. The Splash Meadow runs May to October by day; a low footbridge links it to the East Bank Walk.

places.name: Cottonwood Grove
places.notes: Family picnic tables under young cottonwoods on the east bank, on the East Bank Walk between the Confluence Terrace and the Sink.

places.name: The Upper Wash
places.notes: The wash above the Spring kept exactly as it is: sand, mesquite, Gambel's quail and roadrunners by day, javelina and a coyote on the far bank at dusk; a bench and nothing else.

places.name: Creek Gate
places.notes: The park's gate on Terminal Drive, on the terrace just west of the wash's sand bed: a GENESIS PARK monument, a cobble court and a kiosk, with the westbound Flight Line Tug's bay on the kerb in front of it and the shared eastbound 'Link Plaza and Genesis Park' stop across the road at the drop-off mouth, reached over a raised table. Beyond it the ground drops a metre into cottonwood shade and you see the end of the creek sinking into its cobbles.

places.name: Genesis Stables
places.notes: The horse barn (grey board, 7.5 m) with a tack room and wash rack, facing north onto the Stable Yard; guided trail rides leave the yard on the hour; automatic waterers in the stalls and paddocks instead of open troughs. Wrangler June saddles you up; the Grand Pavilion's wedding carriage leaves the yard by the Carriage Track.

places.name: Riding Arena
places.notes: A 32 m pipe-rail arena: pony rides for small children, lessons, the Saturday gymkhana.

places.name: North horse paddock
places.notes: Turnout paddock with a field shelter and an automatic waterer.

places.name: South horse paddock
places.notes: Turnout paddock nearest the Cottonwood Walk, so walkers see the horses over the rail.

places.name: Landing Run and the Butterfly Meadow
places.notes: The rill that carries the line of the Stage One Landing Wash into the park, rising at the Run Spring beside the Lodge Fountain and joining Genesis Creek at the Confluence, in the low line of a storm swale about 30 m wide between the Cottonwood Walk and the Loop, with the Butterfly Meadow of milkweed, desert marigold and globe mallow in it: monarchs and queens.

places.name: Runway Overlook
places.notes: A 6 m earth knoll, 60 m across at its foot, with a spiral ramp (154 m at about 1 in 25) to a summit of shade sails and stone seats turned east-north-east toward the approach, coin binoculars, an airband speaker and an arrivals board that shows the next jet in: jets show on short final and on the climb-out above the Stage One roofs, and the speaker calls the touchdown behind them. Mostly clean imported fill, with the spoil of the creek, the cistern and the barn pads.

places.name: Overlook Gate
places.notes: Where the Arrivals Walk from the terminal meets the Loop and the Overlook Spur: the GENESIS PARK monument, the kiosk, the Overlook Gate Runnel, and a clump of three Fremont cottonwoods with the copper jet totem that mark the gate from Arrivals Court over the Cart and Bike Hub roof.

promenades.planting: none: desert pavement

trailblazer bollards every 100 m counting the metres round from the Overlook Gate
the Spring Bridge (timber trestle over the creek)
the Run footbridge over the Landing Run
a raised crossing of Airport Park Drive
a low-water crossing of the wash below the Sink
shade trees every 12 m where there were none

promenades.name: Creek Walk

the Sink and the Splash Meadow at its foot

sign_families.description: Section-road monuments at every public gate, 12 to 20 m inside the parcel line (GENESIS ONE wordmark, stage number and name, stage colour band), and pairs of smaller district markers, one at each kerb, at every district entrance.
sign_families.materials: rammed earth wall 6 m by 2.8 m with a corten face plate (monument); 1.8 m corten slab with a stage-colour edge (district marker)
sign_families.colors: Stage One green, Stage Two gold, Stage Three cyan, City airport white

sign_families.description: At every junction of two or more named lines, on a free kerb corner, and at every section-road gate: up to six blades, each giving destination, compass direction, network distance in metres (rounded down to 10) and walking minutes, tipped in the destination's stage colour. Terminal and The Crossing on every Stage One post, Terminal and The Flight Line on every Stage Two post, the Genesis Ring and 'Terminal and Arrivals Court via The Crossing' on every Stage Three post. Any blade whose route uses a tunnel says via The Crossing or via the Flight Line Link.
sign_families.materials: 3.6 m weathered steel post, powder-coated aluminium blades, district finial
sign_families.colors: cream blades with dark text and stage-colour tips

sign_families.description: Street name blades at every junction, including every lane, on the opposite kerb corner from the fingerpost, in the material of the chapter so the sign alone tells you where you are. Street names follow the stage grammar: flight terms in The Landing, market and motor names in The Flight Line, frontier and cosmos names in The Expanse.
sign_families.materials: riveted aluminium (airfield side), painted timber (Old West and Stage Two market), corten (desert modern), edge-lit glass (The Outpost and the Launch Complex)

sign_families.description: You-are-here map totem at the edge of every plaza and at the golf clubhouse, the Threshold Overlook and the Runway Hall: the three-stage staging map, the Horizon Line in white, the brass line marked, shuttle and rover times, and the nearest six destinations with distances.
sign_families.materials: 2.4 m steel and glass totem with a shade cap
sign_families.colors: dark face, stage colours on the map

sign_families.description: Knee-high bronze-capped bollards 1 m inside the promenade edge, every 50 m on the Horizon Line (every 100 m on the other promenades), stamped with the Ring glyph and the distance to the Ring along the line, rounded down to 10 m so the numbers always fall. Beside them runs the brass line: brass studs in the boardwalk edge on Main Street, a brass inlay with a brass star every 25 m elsewhere.
sign_families.materials: bronze-capped concrete bollard, solar lit, steady and downward; brass inlay strip or studs

sign_families.description: One 4 to 5 m identity marker at the heart of each district (never a tower), a silhouette to navigate by.

Airfield-standard signs (yellow on black location, black on yellow direction) at every junction of aircraft pavement, the tunnel portals, the Club Ramp gate and Gate A2, every one at least 20 m from a taxiway centreline (19 m at the two through-the-fence junctions, midway between the parallel taxiway and our taxilane): the design code of the airfield side, seen from the taxiing jet.
sign_families.materials: FAA-style internally lit sign cabinets (on our land or at City-approved spots only)

transit.name: Grand Loop shuttle
transit.mode: electric road shuttle every 15 minutes, all three stages around both runway ends (about 10 km)
stops: Link Plaza and Genesis Park (Terminal Drive, drop-off mouth)
transit.route: Arrivals Court kerb, Landing Boulevard, the Crossing Lane to the Crossing Plaza bay and back, Landing Boulevard, North Gate, North Section Road, Night Field Gate, Night Field Road past the Launch Complex to the Arcade Bay, the Stage Road past the Stagecoach Stop, Corral Road west to the Four Corners bay and back east to Corral Plaza, the Corral Gate, East Section Road, Launch Gate, Ridge Road past the Outpost Gate, Commons Road to Commons Circle, South Gate, South Section Road with the Golf Gate spur, N Airport Rd, Flight Line Gate, the market street at walking pace to Propeller Plaza and back, N Airport Rd, Terminal Drive to the shared Link Plaza and Genesis Park stop on the south kerb at the drop-off mouth, Arrivals Court
transit.notes: It never uses a taxi-street, a taxilane or any aircraft pavement. It serves both portals of The Crossing, so the runway-end route is signed and served from day one if the tunnel is never approved.

transit.name: Crossing Shuttle
transit.mode: electric shuttle through The Crossing every 3 minutes; it boards automatically at both portals, so the tunnel is a ride
transit.notes: The only motor vehicle in the tunnel besides service carts. The moving walkway runs beside it for people who want to walk.

transit.name: Flight Line Tug
transit.mode: vintage airport tug and trailer tram, landside only
transit.notes: Day-one alternative to the Flight Line Link: Terminal Drive and N Airport Rd, no taxiway crossing at any point.

transit.name: Stagecoach
transit.notes: Main Street, the 1928 Strip, the Stage Road and Corral Road: a loop, no dead end. The only wheeled vehicle besides carts and bikes on Main Street.

transit.name: Outpost Rovers
transit.notes: Beyond Ridge Road nothing drives but rovers; the Rover Trail runs the outer edge and the East Range Road links the Launch Complex rovers to The Outpost.

journeys.name: 1. The approach (jet window, about 3 minutes)
steps: Enter from the south-east at about 2,000 ft above the ground over the Sulphur Springs Valley. The first thing on the horizon is the Genesis Ring catching the sun in the far corner of the land, with Runway 03/21 as a grey stroke beyond it, and the real ranges (Mule Mountains west, Perilla Mountains north-east, Sierra San Jose south) around the valley.

Join a left-hand downwind for Runway 21 at about 1,000 ft, heading north-east along the south-east side of the runway. Out of the left window The Expanse passes below in order: The Outpost domes and the Ring inside its Orbit Walk, the Genesis Dome, the compass rose geoglyph at Compass Plaza, the Seven Gates, Main Street's false fronts running straight at the Ring, Four Corners, The Corral, the Launch Complex.

Left base across the open desert north-east of the section. Ahead and to the left: Founders Row with aircraft parked nose-out on the hangar aprons, the Club Hangars, the white peaks of the Grand Pavilion.

Final for Runway 21 across the North Section Road. Left window: the Ring geoglyph laid in coloured gravel at the north tip, then the Launch Complex (its shows hold their lights for you: the Landing Light Pause); the utility yard sits behind a planted berm and the solar field in a screened compound 290 m off the centreline. Right window: Stage One The Landing.
Touchdown near the 21 numbers. The rollout passes over The Crossing (runway signs mark it on both sides), Founders Row on the right, the Expanse Gate and the Genesis Arcade on the left.

journeys.name: 2. Taxi and terminal (about 2 minutes)
steps: Exit at the mid-field connector onto the City's main taxiway, past Hangar Row and the welcome board, and turn north into Gate A2; The Tower stands 120 m to the west. Visiting jets stand on the paved stands beside you.

Airstairs down, 40 m to today's terminal door. Inside, the terminal reads in arrival order: Marcus at Gate A2, Dana at the charter desk, Lupe at Sky Cafe, Officer Dale, Rosa at the desk, and the 1928 wall that points to the Airfield Museum next door.
Out through the new landside door on the north-east end face and 55 m along the Sun Gate Walk, under the Sun Gate shell.

journeys.name: 3. The first five minutes on foot
steps: 0:00 Arrivals Court: the Welcome Fountain, the kiosk map in the three stage colours, the Cart and Bike Hub across the kerb, Sky the tour guide. Across the airfield, 1.3 km away, the Genesis Ring on the horizon. At your feet the brass line starts.

0:30 Four signed choices: north up Landing Boulevard to The Landing Club (green blades); west along the Landside Walk to the Flight Line Link (gold blades, about 0.6 km to Stage Two); west 130 m along the same walk, then north on the Arrivals Walk to Genesis Park (copper blades, and the cottonwoods at its gate in view: the Overlook Gate is 215 m from the court, the water 355 m); north-east along the Club Walk to The Crossing (the brass line).

1:00 The Club Walk: 24 m wide with a central fan palm allee, 15 streamline storefronts under a continuous canopy, the Welcome House at its head; through a gap on the airfield side, the Flight Deck bar where people watch the landings.

2:30 Crossing Plaza: a 1928 biplane on a plinth, a static replica beacon, and the Rabbit's floor jets running toward the tunnel mouth. The portal sign reads [X] THE CROSSING, THE EXPANSE. The Crossing Shuttle is waiting.

3:00 The Crossing: step aboard and ride 467 m, 225 m of it covered, the walls a timeline from the founding of Douglas to the 1928 airfield to the frontier ahead. In the Runway Hall, under the centreline, the LED ceiling shows the jet rolling overhead and the floor hums.

4:30 The shuttle climbs the curved south ramp and you surface facing the Frontier Arch, Main Street and the Genesis Ring dead ahead. The Frontier Well is in front of you, frontier storefronts line the relic 1928 Strip to the left, and the Genesis Arcade stands off your left shoulder on the Night Walk.

journeys.name: 4. The Horizon Line (Arrivals Court to the Ring)
steps: Follow the brass line: 1550 m on the network from Arrivals Court to the Ring, a fountain at every threshold.
Arrivals Court (Welcome Fountain) along the Club Walk arcade to Crossing Plaza (the Rabbit): the 1928 airfield.
The Crossing under Runway 03/21 and the Runway Hall: the threshold between the airfield and the frontier.

Expanse Gate (Frontier Well), under the Frontier Arch, down Upper Main past the stagecoach depot and the trading post to Four Corners (bank, hotel, saloon and general store on its corners), over the Arroyo Bridge, down Lower Main past the courthouse and the assay office to Compass Plaza (Compass Fountain, the Outpost Beacon): the Old West.
Sculpture Avenue through the Seven Gates (Corten Water Table): the desert-modern Design District; the Genesis Lodge and the Field of Light glow to the right after dark.
Outpost Gate on Ridge Road, Countdown ring 10. Beyond this line only rovers and people.

The Countdown through the lit xeno-garden: rings 9 to 2 past Launch Plaza (Launch Mist, the lander 25 m east of the axis), the Genesis Dome and Mission Control; ring 1 stands at the Halo Mist under the Genesis Ring. The Orbit Walk circles it with the eight planet fountains.

journeys.name: 5. To The Flight Line (Stage Two, the aviation stage)
steps: From Arrivals Court take the Landside Walk west past the Link Fountain to Link Plaza (gold blades).
Down the Link ramp, 60 m covered under the main taxiway, up into Propeller Plaza: about 570 m from Arrivals Court.

Propeller Fountain, the Pilot House lounge, the flight school and the maintenance hangar across the apron, the row of four T-hangars, the Flight Line Diner with its tables facing the taxiing aircraft, 6 hangar homes on the Flight Line Taxilane, the Hangar Lane shops and the Giveback Shop, the market street and the Motor Yard beyond.
Day-one alternative: the Flight Line Tug heritage tram from the Arrivals Court kerb along Terminal Drive and N Airport Rd to the Flight Line Gate.

journeys.name: 6. The Grand Loop shuttle (all three stages, about 10 km)
steps: Arrivals Court, the Crossing Plaza bay on the Crossing Lane, the North Gate, the North Section Road around the Runway 21 end.
Night Field Gate, the Launch Complex, the Arcade Bay at the Expanse Gate, the Stagecoach Stop, the Four Corners bay, Corral Plaza, the Corral Gate, the Launch Gate and the Outpost Gate.

The Commons, the South Gate, the Golf Gate, the South Section Road around the Runway 03 end, N Airport Rd, the Flight Line Gate and Propeller Plaza, back along Terminal Drive to the shared Link Plaza and Genesis Park stop at the drop-off mouth and on to Arrivals Court. It never touches a taxi-street.

journeys.name: 7. A night out
steps: Sunset on Sunset Bluff as the jets land into the glow.
Dinner on Main Street, a round at the Four Corners Saloon, the upstairs loft windows lit.
The Night Walk past the Arcade doors to the Launch Complex: the Crater Bowl, the Landing Light Pause when a jet comes in, the Star Cinema next door, the vendor village around the countdown clock.
The Field of Light on the way back, the last rover to The Outpost, the Ring lit cyan; then the dark-sky hour, when the Ring and the Countdown dim to a minimum for the Dark Sky Observatory.

journeys.name: 8. A Founders Row morning (resident)
steps: Coffee on the house side of the hangar home on Propeller Way; the hangar door rolls up onto the residents' taxi-street.
Taxi down Propeller Way, hold short at the Landing Taxilane, through TTF-2 onto the City parallel taxiway (a City-designated access point), and away off Runway 03.
Back by lunch: park on the Club Ramp and walk into the clubhouse.

journeys.name: 9. Arriving by road from Douglas
steps: From 1100 N Airport Rd, Terminal Drive to the Arrivals Court kerb, or 340 m south to the Flight Line Gate for Stage Two. Genesis Park is the City's Airport Park entrance the town already uses, at the Airport Park Drive gate 210 m north of Terminal Drive, or the South car park off Terminal Drive.

For The Expanse by car: the North Section Road to the Night Field Gate (Launch Complex car park and the Arcade Bay), or the East Section Road to the Corral Gate for the town. Cars stop at the gates, the car parks and the bays; Main Street and the Expanse Gate are for people, carts, bikes and the stagecoach.

journeys.name: 10. Genesis Park (off the jet and into the water, about 45 minutes)
steps: From Arrivals Court the cottonwood clump and the copper jet totem at the Overlook Gate show over the Cart and Bike Hub roof. Take the Landside Walk west 130 m to the copper-tipped GENESIS PARK fingerpost, turn right onto the Arrivals Walk under the palo verdes, cross Terminal Drive on the raised table and arrive at the Overlook Gate: 215 m, about 3 minutes. The Flight Line Tug stops at the Creek Gate bay and the Grand Loop at the Link Plaza and Genesis Park stop across the road; the Creek Gate is 144 m from Link Plaza.

Climb the Overlook Spur one and a quarter times round the knoll to the summit (177 m on the ramp, never steeper than 1 in 25). The seats face east-north-east toward the approach; the arrivals board says a jet is four minutes out. It appears low over the North Section Road on short final for Runway 21 and slides down behind the Stage One roofs, and the airband speaker calls the touchdown; a few minutes later a departure climbs out over the same roofs.

Down the knoll and round the Loop to the Confluence Terrace, then down the East Bank Walk under the young cottonwoods, over the Splash Meadow footbridge to the Splash Meadow (353 m from the summit): the ground jets fire and children dam their own play stream with the sluice gates on the terrace, while beside it the creek runs clear over its cobbles and, a few metres on, sinks into the ground at the Sink, as desert streams do.

Up the Creek Walk under the cottonwoods: the Mesquite Steps, the Cottonwood Grove across the water, then the Confluence, where the Landing Run comes in from Stage One under the Confluence Bridge and Cottonwood Falls pours over its basalt just upstream (132 m from the Splash Meadow to the Confluence Terrace).

Out across the Sacaton Meadow on the boardwalk, where the creek runs in one narrow planted channel through tall bunchgrass (the Sacaton loop is 263 m), and on up through Willow Reach, dragonflies over the riffles, to Genesis Spring welling up out of its grotto (311 m from the Splash Meadow).

Across the Loop and in by the Farm Gate Walk to Genesis Farm: the Barnyard is 240 m from the Spring. Feed the goats from a cup bought at the Farm Stand, work the Barnyard Pump, watch the horses at Genesis Stables across the creek (138 m from the Spring by the Stable Walk).

Down the Farm Walk to Windmill Green and the Hangar Playground (138 m), then east on the Cottonwood Walk over the Confluence Bridge and along the Landing Run to the Stage One Wash Walk (262 m), or back round the Loop to the Overlook Gate and Arrivals Court (519 m).

On a Saturday the town side is full: Little League on Field 2, under-10 soccer either side of the Bandshell Walk, the farm market in the Barnyard, a birthday in a Mesquite Grove ramada; Field 1 under the lights at 7 pm and a Bandshell concert at dusk. The creek runs until the lanterns dim at 10 pm and drains away overnight. On a monsoon afternoon the creek pumps shut off, amber beacons close the Riffle Stones and the low-water crossings, and the real wash runs brown bank to bank for an hour under the bridges before the creek comes back on, clear, from the Spring.

engine.zones: replace the six zone circles with the three parcel polygons (S1, S2, S3) plus the City airport polygon
engine.signs: bake all sign text into 2 to 4 texture atlases, instance each sign family, draw text only within about 60 m of the player
engine.tunnels: lower the terrain only under the open ramps; build each covered box as a separate interior with its own floor height, an in-tunnel flag at the ramp foot, the camera clamped to the box and its own navigation segment; the Crossing Shuttle ride is the fallback if the interior slips

genesis_park.terrain: raise the knoll (a 6 m truncated cone, foot radius 30 m, summit radius 8 m) and cut the creek, the Run and its storm swale 0.3 m into the wash bed; nothing else changes grade
genesis_park.water: one animated water ribbon each on the creek and the Run polylines (running 07:00 to 22:00, drained overnight), foam sprites at the three cascades, ground-jet particles at the Splash Meadow terrace and the splash pad; the audio bed switches to running water within 60 m of the water; a Monsoon Day weather event floods the wash bank to bank for an hour with the creek pumps off
genesis_park.animals: farm animals wander inside their paddock polygons on a simple steering loop and sleep in the barns at night; goats follow a player holding a feed cup, chickens scatter from a running player, the farm dog herds the sheep in at dusk; the trail-ride horses follow the Trail Ride Loop polyline; the wedding carriage runs the Carriage Track on event days
genesis_park.lights: field lights on a Friday and Saturday night schedule, off by 22:00; the Bandshell's stage glow only during events; the Loop's solar lanterns steady, shielded and downward, dimmed at 22:00 with the creek and Cottonwood Falls

water.name: Genesis Creek
water.width_note: wider over the riffles, one narrow planted channel through the Sacaton Meadow, narrow in the runs
water.depth_m: 0.05 to 0.2, never deeper, so there is no still pool anywhere; water to watch, not to wade in (the Splash Meadow is the play water)
water.fall_m: about 4 end to end, read as the wash's general grade (to be confirmed by a topographic survey; if the wash is flatter the cascades get lower and the pump does the rest)
water.bed: a sealed clay and liner bed under 30 cm of local river cobble, keyed into the existing low-flow channel with cobble riffles and three stacked-stone cascades, armoured at every crossing so monsoon floods pass over it, with deergrass and big sacaton planted to the water's edge on both banks
water.treatment: filtration and UV only, no chlorine (so the dragonflies and the planting do well); no wading except the Riffle Stones crossing
water.hours: 7 am until the 10 pm lantern dimming, then drained to the cistern every night without exception, on freezing nights and before storms
reaches: the Spring to the Spring Bridge: fast shallow water over cobble below the grotto, then the Spring Steps
braided riffles and gravel bars under Goodding willow, bunchgrass to the edge; the Riffle Stones
one narrow planted channel through the drip-watered Sacaton Meadow under the Sacaton Boardwalk and the Willow Bridge
one channel under the tallest cottonwoods: Cottonwood Falls, the Confluence Bridge and the Confluence with the Landing Run
riffles and short runs past the Cottonwood Grove and the Mesquite Steps, the East Bank Walk opposite the Creek Walk
past the Splash Meadow terrace behind a low planted bank, then the creek fans out over a cobble bar and sinks into the ground

water.name: Landing Run
water.source: the Run Spring, a stone spout 13 m from the Stage One Lodge Fountain (separate water systems)
water.character: a narrow rill down the line of the Stage One Landing Wash, in the low line of the 30 m storm swale between the Cottonwood Walk and the Loop, lined with desert willow and milkweed

water.name: return mains (buried)
water.notes: about 350 m of buried pipe from the pump room up the west bank to the Spring, with a branch under the Cottonwood Walk to the Run Spring

water.name: cistern
water.notes: holds everything in the creek loop (about 90 cubic metres) so the creek and the Run drain down every night without exception and before storms

water.name: pump room and treatment
water.notes: two separate systems in the Splash Meadow House: the creek loop (filtration and UV only, no chlorine, a pump of about 3 kW lifting 30 litres a second about 6 m, the fall plus the pipe run; make-up water on a meter) and the Splash Meadow's own sealed splash-pad circuit (filtration, UV and chlorine to public splash-pad rules, a 20 cubic metre tank), never mixed

water.name: Splash Meadow tank
water.notes: the Splash Meadow's own sealed and treated circuit, like the Propeller Splash Pad's; drained daily

water.name: Genesis Pond (option, not in the plan)
water.notes: decision 14, option B: a lined 0.3 ha still pond in place of the Splash Meadow terrace; not recommended beside an active runway

water.name: Monsoon basin (option)
water.notes: decision 14, option C: the low ground by the Sink graded as a planted meadow that holds storm water for a day or two and drains within 48 hours

landscape.name: Sacaton Meadow
landscape.note: a drip-watered bunchgrass meadow of big sacaton and deergrass: the creek crosses it in one narrow planted channel; no sedges, no wetland plants, no wet ground and no ponded water, kept tall and dense

landscape.name: Riparian gallery
landscape.note: Fremont cottonwood, Goodding willow, Arizona sycamore and desert willow on drip along the creek (trees set back from the walk surfaces), deergrass and big sacaton planted to the water's edge on every reach outside the Riffle Stones, the bridges and the Splash Meadow; desert willow and milkweed only along the Landing Run, kept under 8 m

landscape.name: Butterfly Meadow
landscape.note: milkweed, desert marigold and globe mallow along the Landing Run: monarchs and queens

landscape.name: Landing Wash storm swale
landscape.note: about 30 m between the Cottonwood Walk and the Loop, with the Landing Run in its low line: the Stage One Landing Wash's monsoon flow comes in through two box culverts and reaches Genesis Creek at the Confluence; bunchgrass and milkweed, flooded for an hour after a storm

landscape.name: The Great Lawn (kept turf)
landscape.note: the City's existing grass field kept as turf, mowed short, a youth soccer pitch either side of the Bandshell Walk, which crosses it flush with the turf; open to walk across

landscape.name: Field 1 (kept)
landscape.note: the City's baseball diamond, skinned infield and outfield kept; home plate at (-448,-442), the first-base line along z -442

landscape.name: Field 2 and the North Meadow
landscape.note: the rough practice field restored to even turf, Field 2 laid out with home plate at its south-east corner facing north-west, its outfield backing onto Field 1's across the Fields Walk

landscape.name: Pump Track
landscape.note: asphalt rollers and berms on the line of the old dirt track

landscape.name: Runway Overlook knoll
landscape.note: a 6 m truncated cone, foot radius 30 m, summit radius 8 m, about 7,500 cubic metres, mostly clean imported fill (the creek, cistern and barn pad spoil gives about 1,000)

landscape.name: Airport Park car park (kept)
landscape.note: resurfaced, shade trees in new planted islands (the fingerposts and blades stand on the islands at the Bandshell Lane and Fields Walk mouths)

landscape.name: Airport Park car park west island
landscape.note: the car park's west 14 m rebuilt as a planted island that carries the Loop, with one raised crossing of Airport Park Drive

landscape.name: South car park
landscape.note: the dirt lot paved as about 40 spaces north of the realigned Terminal Drive, entered by the South Lot Lane

landscape.name: North car park
landscape.note: about 20 spaces on the old gravel strip, inside the City's parcel line and 6 m clear of the Loop; planted islands at the lane mouth

landscape.name: Terminal Drive screen planting
landscape.note: a mesquite and desert willow hedge between Terminal Drive and the park, broken at the Creek Gate and the Overlook Gate

props.name: Riffle Stones
props.note: flat-topped basalt stepping stones 60 cm apart over a riffle 10 cm deep, from the creek rock kit; the one place the creek is crossed on stones; closed by amber beacons when the creek is off

props.name: Spring Bridge
props.note: a timber trestle over the creek just below Genesis Spring, 1.5 m over the bed so monsoon flows pass under it

props.name: Confluence Bridge
props.note: a riveted steel truss (a nod to the 1928 hangars) carrying the Cottonwood Walk over the creek just above the Confluence, with Cottonwood Falls upstream; on abutments above the flood line

props.name: Splash Meadow footbridge
props.note: a low timber span of the boardwalk kit from the East Bank Walk to the Splash Meadow, so nobody wades the creek to reach the play water

props.name: Willow Bridge
props.note: a straight timber span of the boardwalk kit, level with the Sacaton Boardwalk

props.name: Run footbridge
props.note: a short timber span of the boardwalk kit carrying the Loop over the Landing Run

props.name: Genesis Spring grotto
props.note: stacked basalt and limestone 4 m high with a fern and monkeyflower seep face; the spring boil at its mouth

props.name: The Sink cobble bar
props.note: the creek fans out and sinks into a cobble bar over the collection gallery (creek rock kit)

props.name: Splash Meadow terrace
props.note: a flat stone terrace on the west bank with ground jets, stepping stones, hand pumps and sluice gates on its own sealed, treated splash-pad circuit; the creek runs past its east edge behind a low planted bank and a rail (Blender kit from existing boulders; the jets are procedural)

props.name: The Little Hangar
props.note: a bow-truss climbing frame with slides and a rope net at the heart of the Hangar Playground

props.name: Climb-aboard 1928 biplane
props.note: the master plan's 1928 biplane model (Crossing Plaza) re-used at play scale with a climbing frame and soft fall surfacing

props.name: Field 1 grandstand
props.note: 300 seats under a shade roof laid along Field 1's first-base line on the foul side, 36 by 8 m, 5 m off the line and clear of the infield, 3.5 m from the scorers' booth and 13 m from the car park; its back on the Ballpark Walk (from the Corral and Cart Course stand builders)

props.name: Field 2 bleachers (third-base line)
props.note: aluminium bleachers on the foul side of Field 2's third-base line

props.name: Windmill Green west ramada (City, kept)
props.note: the City's white shade ramada read from the aerial at x -237..-228, z -369..-361, kept and re-roofed as a Windmill Green shelter; the Cottonwood Walk and the Lawn Walk pass beside it

props.name: Windmill Green east ramada (City, kept)

props.name: Splash-court ramada (City, kept)

props.note: an armoured, flush concrete-and-cobble crossing where the Loop's south leg crosses the wash's sand bed below the Sink, built to be over-topped by a monsoon flow; closed by amber beacons while the wash runs

props.name: Creek Walk low-water crossing
